passage_text: Researchers investigated the effect of a novel antihypertensive drug on systolic blood pressure (SBP) in adults aged 45–65. In a randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial, 240 participants were assigned to one of four groups: placebo (n=60), low dose (10 mg, n=60), medium dose (20 mg, n=60), or high dose (40 mg, n=60). SBP was measured at baseline and after 12 weeks of treatment. The mean SBP reduction (± SD) for each group was: placebo 2.1 ± 5.3 mmHg, 10 mg 8.4 ± 6.1 mmHg, 20 mg 12.7 ± 5.9 mmHg, 40 mg 15.3 ± 6.4 mmHg. Table 1 summarizes these findings along with p‑values and 95 % confidence intervals for each dose comparison versus placebo.
table_data:
Table 1: SBP Reduction by Dose
Dose (mg) | Mean Reduction (mmHg) | SD | p‑value vs placebo | 95% CI of difference vs placebo
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
Placebo | 2.1 | 5.3 | — | —
10 | 8.4 | 6.1 | <0.0001 | 4.2–8.4
20 | 12.7 | 5.9 | <0.0001 | 8.6–12.6
40 | 15.3 | 6.4 | <0.0001 | 11.1–15.3
stem: Which statement best reflects the data presented in Table 1?

options.A: The 10 mg dose produced a statistically significant SBP reduction compared to placebo.
options.B: The 20 mg dose had the largest mean SBP reduction but the widest confidence interval.
options.C: The 40 mg dose produced a smaller mean SBP reduction than the 20 mg dose.
options.D: The placebo group showed no change in SBP.

explanation: Correct: A) The 10 mg group had a mean reduction of 8.4 mmHg versus 2.1 mmHg for placebo, with p < 0.0001 and a 95% CI for the difference (4.2-8.4 mmHg) that excludes zero. Why the others are wrong: B) The 40 mg dose, not the 20 mg dose, had the largest mean reduction (15.3 mmHg). C) The 40 mg mean reduction (15.3) is larger than the 20 mg mean (12.7). D) The placebo group had a mean reduction of 2.1 mmHg.
trap: Picking the 20 mg group as the largest effect, or assuming placebo means zero change.

stem: What is the main purpose of the placebo group’s 2.1 mmHg mean SBP reduction in interpreting the drug groups’ results?

options.A: It estimates the SBP change that occurs without the drug, so drug effects are judged relative to it.
options.B: It shows the drug raised SBP in treated participants.
options.D: It shows placebo was as effective as the 10 mg dose.

explanation: Correct: A) The placebo arm shows the change that occurs with no active drug (expectation, measurement variation, regression to the mean), so the drug effect is the difference from placebo. Why the others are wrong: B) The drug groups’ SBP fell more than placebo, not rose. C) A small placebo response says nothing about failed blinding. D) The 10 mg reduction (8.4 mmHg) was significantly larger than placebo (p < 0.0001).
trap: Reading any change in the placebo group as evidence that the drug had no effect.

stem: What is the difference in mean SBP reduction between the 20 mg dose and placebo?
explanation: Correct: B) 12.7 - 2.1 = 10.6 mmHg. Why the others are wrong: A) 2.6 mmHg is the difference between the 40 mg and 20 mg groups (15.3 - 12.7), not 20 mg vs placebo. C) 12.7 mmHg is the 20 mg mean reduction alone, without subtracting placebo. D) 15.3 mmHg is the 40 mg mean reduction.
trap: Reporting the 20 mg group’s own mean reduction instead of subtracting the placebo reduction.

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the data?

options.A: Higher doses are associated with greater SBP reductions.
options.B: The 10 mg group showed a larger mean SBP reduction than the placebo group.
options.C: The 40 mg dose has the highest mean reduction but also the widest SD.
options.D: The 20 mg dose produced a larger mean SBP reduction than the 40 mg dose.

explanation: Mean reductions rise with dose (2.1, 8.4, 12.7, 15.3 mmHg), so A, B and C are supported (the 40 mg SD of 6.4 is the largest). D is not supported: the 20 mg mean (12.7) is lower than the 40 mg mean (15.3).
trap: Choosing C because the highest dose seems to deserve the smallest variability; the 40 mg SD (6.4) is in fact the largest.

stem: Which statement best describes the dose–response pattern in Table 1?

options.A: Mean SBP reduction rose with each dose, but each step added less: 4.3 mmHg from 10 to 20 mg and 2.6 mmHg from 20 to 40 mg.
options.B: Mean SBP reduction was directly proportional to dose.
options.C: The 10 mg dose produced a smaller mean reduction than placebo.
options.D: The 40 mg dose produced a smaller mean reduction than the 20 mg dose.

explanation: Correct: A) Means were 2.1, 8.4, 12.7 and 15.3 mmHg; the increments from 10 to 20 mg (4.3) and 20 to 40 mg (2.6) are smaller than the first step (6.3), although the dose doubled each time. Why the others are wrong: B) Doubling the dose from 10 to 20 mg did not double the effect (8.4 to 12.7). C) The 10 mg reduction (8.4) exceeded placebo (2.1). D) The 40 mg mean (15.3) exceeded the 20 mg mean (12.7).
trap: Assuming a doubled dose gives a doubled effect, or that the largest dose must be best or worst.
